h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן, מַאֲמָר ג׳ Rosh Chodesh Nisan — Maamar Gimmel

p: בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה
In Sefer Yetzirah:
הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת ה' בְּשִׂיחָה וְכוּלֵּי וְנִיסָן בַּשָּׁנָה וְרֶגֶל יָמִין בַּנֶּפֶשׁ וְכוּלֵּי
"He made the letter Hei king in speech, etc., and Nisan in the year, and the right foot in the soul, etc."
כֵּן הוּא גִּירְסַת הָאֲרִיזַ"ל.
such is the textual reading of the Arizal.
ה' תַּתָּאָה שְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה מַלְכוּת,
The lower Hei is the lower Shechinah, Malchus,
וּבְנִיסָן הַתְחָלַת בִּנְיַן אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית,
and in Nisan was the beginning of the building of the Israelite nation,
וְזֶה בְּה' בְּרָאָם
and this is "with Hei He created them"
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר).
(and this has been explained elsewhere).
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין כֹּחָם אֶלָּא בְּפִיהֶם,
And Israel's strength is solely in their mouth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
(תַּנְחוּמָא בְּשַׁלַּח ט')
(Tanchuma Beshalach 9):
לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְתוֹלַעַת וְכוּלֵּי.
"Why are Israel compared to a worm, etc.?"
וְזֶה הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב,
And this is "The voice is the voice of Yaakov"
קֹל ה' תְּפִלָּה, קוֹל ו' תּוֹרָה.
kol with Hei is prayer, kol with Vav is Torah.
וְאָמַר בְּשִׂיחָה וְלֹא אָמַר בְּדִבּוּר,
And it said "in sichah" and did not say "in dibbur,"
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
based on what they said
(עֵירוּבִין נ"ד:)
(Eruvin 54b):
"שִׂיחוּ" אֵלּוּ בַּעֲלֵי תַּלְמוּד שֶׁכָּל שִׂיחָתָן דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
"'Converse'—these are the masters of Talmud, for all their conversation is words of Torah,"
וּבַעֲלֵי תַּלְמוּד הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהֵם מְבוּלָּסִין בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and "masters of Talmud" refers to when they are thoroughly mixed with words of Torah,
וְאָז שִׂיחָתָן תּוֹרָה.
and then their very conversation is Torah.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ רֶגֶל יָמִין,
And what they said, "the right foot,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
is along the lines of what is stated:
אַשְׁרֵי תְמִימֵי דָרֶךְ הַהֹלְכִים בְּתוֹרַת ה'
"Fortunate are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the Torah of Hashem"
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל).
(as explained above).
וְהָעִיקַּר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּ"לֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ",
And the main thing is that words of Torah be in "a wise man's heart at his right,"
שֶׁרַק אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל הוּצְרְכוּ לְ"רֹב חָכְמָה" לְתַקֵּן הָ"רֹב כַּעַס",
for only after the sin were they in need of "an abundance of wisdom" to rectify the "abundance of anger,"
לְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִ"לֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ",
to empty out the evil from "a fool's heart at his left,"
שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא חָטְאוּ לֹא נִיתַּן לָהֶם אֶלָּא חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה
for had they not sinned, they would have been given only the Five Books of the Torah
(נְדָרִים כ"ב:)
(Nedarim 22b).
כֵּן הוּא גִּירְסַת הָאֲרִיזַ"ל.
Such is the reading of the Arizal.
וְגִירְסַת הַגְּאוֹנִים:
Whereas the reading of the Geonim is:
הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת ה' בִּרְאִיָּה וְנִיסָן בַּשָּׁנָה וְכָבֵד בַּנֶּפֶשׁ.
"He made the letter Hei king in sight, and Nisan in the year, and the liver in the soul."
וְהַיְינוּ דִּרְאִיָּה אוֹתִיּוֹת יִרְאָה,
And this is because "re'iyah" (sight) has the same letters as "yirah" (fear),
וְהַיְינוּ ה' תַּתָּאָה:
which is the lower Hei:
שַׁבָּת דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא אִיהִי יִרְאָה וְשַׁרְיָא בַּהּ יִרְאָה
"The Shabbos of Friday night is fear, and fear rests upon it"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א' ה':).
(Zohar, Vol. 1, 5b).
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים עוֹמֵד עָלָיו וְרוֹאֶה בְּמַעֲשָׂיו,
That is, when a person sees that the King of kings stands over him and observes his deeds,
מִיָּד יַגִּיעַ אֵלָיו הַיִּרְאָה
immediately fear comes upon him
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים).
(as has been explained many times).
אַךְ מַה הַשַּׁיָּיכוּת לְכָבֵד בַּנֶּפֶשׁ?
Yet what is the connection to "the liver in the soul"?
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
It is according to what they said
(בְּרָכוֹת ס"א:)
(Berachos 61b):
כָּבֵד כּוֹעֵס.
"The liver grows angry."
וּמָצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
And we find in the Gemara
(נְדָרִים שָׁם)
(Nedarim, ibid.):
אִלְמָלֵא חָטְאוּ וְכוּלֵּי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"Had they not sinned, etc., as it is said
(קֹהֶלֶת א', י"ח)
(Koheles 1:18):
כִּי בְּרֹב חָכְמָה רָב כָּעַס,
'For in much wisdom is much anger,'"
מְכוּנֶּה כָּל הַחֲטָאִים בְּשֵׁם כַּעַס.
all sins are referred to by the term "anger."
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ
And so they said
(נְדָרִים כ"ב.)
(Nedarim 22a):
כָּל הַכּוֹעֵס כָּל מִינֵי גֵיהִנּוֹם שׁוֹלְטִין בּוֹ.
"Whoever becomes angry, all kinds of Gehinnom rule over him."
הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁלֹשׁ קְלִיפּוֹת: הַקִּנְאָה וְהַתַּאֲוָה וְהַכָּבוֹד,
That is, although there are three husks—envy, lust, and honor
אֲבָל שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַקְּלִיפּוֹת הוּא הַכַּעַס, קְלִיפַּת עֵשָׂו,
nevertheless, the root of all the husks is anger, the husk of Esav,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה לֹא יוּשְׁאַר כְּלָל לֶעָתִיד,
of which nothing at all will remain in the future,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(עוֹבַדְיָה א', י"ח)
(Ovadyah 1:18):
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה שָׂרִיד לְבֵית עֵשָׂו.
"And there shall be no survivor to the House of Esav."
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קְלִיפַּת הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁיּוּשְׁאַר לֶעָתִיד,
Not so the husk of lust, which will remain in the future,
רַק יִהְיֶה לְטוֹב לִהְיוֹת חֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא,
only it will be transformed for good to become a yearning for Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר
as brought in the Zohar
(חֵלֶק א' מִדְרָשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם קל"ח.),
(Vol. 1, Midrash HaNe'elam 138a).
וְכֵן כָּבוֹד יֵשׁ לְטוֹב,
And similarly, there is a positive aspect to honor,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב' י"ז, ו')
(II Divrei HaYamim 17:6):
וַיִּגְבַּהּ לִבּוֹ בְּדַרְכֵי ה'.
"And his heart was elevated in the ways of Hashem."
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַכַּעַס, אֵין בּוֹ לְטוֹב כְּלָל.
Not so anger—there is nothing good in it at all.
וְלָמָּה נִבְרָא הָאֵבֶר הַמְרוּמָּז נֶגְדּוֹ שֶׁהוּא הַכָּבֵד?
Why, then, was the organ corresponding to it—namely, the liver—created?
רַק כְּנֶגֶד עֲמָלֵק דִּכְתִיב בּוֹ
Solely to be directed against Amalek, of whom it is written
(דְּבָרִים כ"ה, י"ט)
(Devarim 25:19):
מָחֹה תִמְחֶה.
"You shall surely blot out."
וְכֵן לְהִתְאַכְזֵר עַל הָרְשָׁעִים כְּמוֹ בְּעִיר הַנִּדַּחַת,
And similarly, to act harshly against the wicked, as in the case of the subverted city (Ir HaNidachas),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ רַחֲמִים גְּמוּרִים,
which is complete mercy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּפָרָשַׁת עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת
as it is said in the section of the subverted city
(שָׁם י"ג, י"ח)
וְנָתַן לְךָ רַחֲמִים וְרִחַמְךָ וְגוֹמֵר.
"And He will grant you mercy and have mercy upon you, etc."
רַק הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מְפַתֶּה אֶת הָאָדָם
Only, the evil inclination entices a person
וּמַרְאֶה לוֹ שֶׁזֶּה כַּעַס שֶׁל מִצְוָה.
and makes it appear to him as though it is righteous indignation.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר
And concerning this it is said
(שְׁמוֹת ל"ה, ג')
(Shemos 35:3):
לֹא תְבַעֲרוּ אֵשׁ בְּכֹל מֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
"You shall not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Shabbos day,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא
and as brought
(תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן מ"ח)
(Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48):
דְּלָא אִתְקָרֵב תַּמָּן עֲצִיבוּ דִּטְחוֹל וְכַעַס דְּמָרָה.
"That the melancholy of the spleen and the anger of the gall/liver should not approach there."
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּכֹל מֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם,
And this is why it says "in any of your dwellings"
הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע יְסַמֵּא אֶת הָעֵינַיִם שֶׁזֶּה כַּעַס דִּקְדוּשָּׁה, רוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנַן,
meaning even when the evil inclination blinds the eyes to think it is holy anger, "the anger of the Sages,"
דְּאִיהִי טַב לְכָל סִטְרִין
which is good for all sides
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' קפ"ב:),
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 182b)
אֲבָל תֵּדַע שֶׁהוּא עֲצַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
know that it is the counsel of the evil inclination,
שֶׁאָמַר לָרַע טוֹב וְשָׂם חֹשֶׁךְ לְאוֹר,
which calls evil good and substitutes darkness for light,
וְהוּא מְסַמֵּא הָרְאִיָּה שֶׁהִיא הַיִּרְאָה מִמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הָעוֹמֵד עָלָיו.
and blinds the sight, which is the fear of the King of kings standing over him.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת ה' בִּרְאִיָּה וְנִיסָן בַּשָּׁנָה,
And this is what they said: "He made the letter Hei king in sight, and Nisan in the year,"
שֶׁבּוֹ נִבְנָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
in which Knesses Yisrael was built.
וְאַף שֶׁאַחַר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה הַקִּטְרוּג גַּם כֵּן,
And although after the Exodus from Egypt there was also heavenly prosecution,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
as they said in Midrash Rabbah
(וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ"א, ד')
(Vayikra Rabbah 21:4),
וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ק"ע:)
וּבַמְּכִילְתָּא
and in the Mechilta
(Beshalach 6):
"וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חֹמָה" חָסֵר,
"'And the waters were a wall (chomah) for them'—spelled deficiently without a Vav (chemah),"
שֶׁהָיָה חֵמָה וְקֶצֶף קִטְרוּג עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
indicating there was wrath (chemah) and anger prosecuting Israel,
עִם כָּל זֶה בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף זָכוּ לִרְאִיָּה,
nevertheless, at the Splitting of the Sea they merited sight,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
(מְכִילְתָּא בְּשַׁלַּח הַשִּׁירָה ג' וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שָׁם ס'.):
(Mechilta Beshalach, Shirah 3, and the holy Zohar, ibid. 60a):
רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה יְחֶזְקֵאל.
"A maidservant saw at the Sea what Yechezkel did not see."
וְכֵן כְּתִיב
And so it is written
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, ל"א):
(Shemos 14:31):
וַיִּרְאוּ הָעָם אֶת ה' וְגוֹמֵר
"And the people feared Hashem, etc."
יִרְאָה אוֹתִיּוֹת רְאִיָּה,
fear (yirah) has the letters of sight (re'iyah),
אֱמוּנָה אִיהִי אֱמוּנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר
faith, "She is faith," as brought in the Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' ר"ל.).
וְכָבֵד בַּנֶּפֶשׁ
And "the liver in the soul"
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַכַּעַס רַק כְּנֶגֶד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, קְלִיפַּת עֲמָלֵק יִצְרָא בִּישָׁא,
means that anger should be directed solely against the evil inclination, the husk of Amalek, the evil inclination,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר
as brought in the Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' ק"ס.)
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: מָחֹה תִמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק.
as it is said: "You shall surely blot out the remembrance of Amalek."
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לֹא תְבַעֲרוּ וְגוֹמֵר בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
And this is what is said: "You shall not kindle, etc., on the Shabbos day,"
שֶׁאָז יְכוֹלִין לִזְכּוֹת לְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה דְּאִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִתַּמָּן,
for then one can merit the Supernal Shabbos from which the evil inclination is removed,
וְאָז הַכָּבֵד רַק לְרוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנַן דְּאִיהוּ טַב לְכָל סִטְרִין
and then the liver is used only for the anger of the Sages, which is good for all sides
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר).
(and this has been explained elsewhere).
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן הַמְכוּוָּן לְגִירְסַת הָאֲרִיזַ"ל רֶגֶל יָמִין,
And this is also the intent of the Arizal's reading, "the right foot":
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה כְּלָל לֵב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ,
that there should be no "fool's heart at his left" at all,
רַק הֹלְכֵי בְּתוֹרַת ה' שֶׁנִּקְרָא רֶגֶל יָמִין.
only "those who walk in the Torah of Hashem," which is called the right foot.
וְזוֹכִין לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי שִׂיחָה, תְּפִלָּה וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And one merits this through sichah—prayer and the Oral Torah
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ל"ח, ד'):
(Shemos Rabbah 38:4):
קְחוּ עִמָּכֶם דְּבָרִים וְכוּלֵּי וְאֵין דְּבָרִים אֶלָּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵּי
"'Take with you words (devarim), etc.'—and 'words' means nothing other than words of Torah, etc.;
אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין;
they said to Him: 'We do not know [Torah]';
אָמַר לָהֶם: בְּכוּ וְהִתְפַּלְּלוּ לְפָנַי וְכוּלֵּי.
He said to them: 'Weep and pray before Me, etc.'"
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה יְכוֹלִים לִזְכּוֹת לְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל
For through Torah and prayer one can merit to empty out the evil from the fool's heart,
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה רַק לֵב אֶחָד לְאָבִינוּ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם,
so that there is only one unified heart directed to our Father in Heaven,
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה כַּעַס כְּלָל רַק רוּגְזָא דִּקְדוּשָּׁה דְּטַב לְכָל סִטְרִין.
and there is no anger at all except holy indignation, which is good for all sides.
וְזֶה עֵסֶק חֹדֶשׁ זֶה:
And this is the spiritual work of this month:
מִשְׁכוּ וּקְחוּ, שֶׁהוּא סוּר מֵרָע וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeitzei 7 — “Envy and anger are the trait of Esav, which has no rectification at all, even in the future, as it says, ‘There shall be no remnant.’ And although we find that ‘the anger of the Sages is good’ to give honor to the Torah, that is only in this world, so long as the seed of Amalek exists; therefore anger is sometimes needed against his side. But in the future, when the seed of Amalek is destroyed, nothing of it will remain. Therefore the metzora is sent even from the camp of Israel, for this trait has no ascent in holiness, unlike the zav, corresponding to desire, which ascends as yearning for Torah.” Connection: Both set anger apart from desire as having no good side; Vayeitzei 7 adds that even holy anger exists only while Amalek does, and grounds the distinction in the metzora and the zav.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Elimelech of Lizhensk, Noam Elimelech, Tzav — “‘And he shall lift up the ashes that the fire has consumed’: it is impossible for a person to break all the traits born with him from his mother's womb; rather, he must lift them up to holiness. For example, one who has the trait of anger should turn away from outer anger and be angry at the wicked, and so with every trait. ‘And he shall take off his garments and put on other garments’: afterward he reaches a higher level, until he is stripped entirely of all the traits. ‘And carry the ashes outside the camp’: nothing of his inborn traits will ever come to him again, but all will be in great holiness.” Connection: Both allow anger only as turned against the wicked; Noam Elimelech adds that this redirection is a first stage of avodah, leading to a level where the inborn trait is removed entirely.
